---
title: "Atlas spaces and transforms"
---

A coordinate names a place in the brain only together with its space: the atlas, the origin,
the units and the scaling it was recorded in. This page explains the spaces of the IBL atlas
and how they relate. To cite an atlas or a scaling, see [Citations](../citations.qmd).

## The Allen CCF frame and the IBL frame

The Allen Common Coordinate Framework (CCF) is a volume, and the IBL frame is a way of writing
positions in that same volume. Every coordinate in the IBL atlas is in the IBL frame. The two
frames differ in where the origin is, what the units are, and which way each axis counts
(@fig-frames).

![The Allen CCF frame beside the IBL frame, on the same sagittal template slice. In the CCF the
origin is the corner of the volume; in the IBL frame it is bregma.](images/frames-allen-vs-ibl.svg){#fig-frames fig-alt="The same side view of the mouse brain twice, anterior on the left, inside the box that is the atlas volume. In the Allen CCF the origin is the anterior, dorsal, left corner, in micrometres, with AP increasing towards posterior and DV towards ventral. In the IBL frame the origin is bregma, in metres, with AP increasing towards anterior and DV towards dorsal."}

Bregma sits at ML 5739, AP 5400, DV 332 µm in the CCF volume. The signs and units of the IBL
frame are on [Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd).

The CCF is mirror-symmetric about ML 5695 µm, 44 µm medial of bregma, at every resolution.
To mirror points between hemispheres, reflect about `atlas.midline_x` (in metres, relative to the
origin of the atlas frame, which is bregma for the Allen atlases but not for every atlas), not about x = 0.

@tbl-midline shows how that plane was found. Each volume was mirrored about a range of ML positions
and the two sides compared, with the Jaccard overlap of the brain masks and the correlation of the
template intensities (1 is a perfect mirror image). The positions are in CCF µm, the volume index
times the resolution, as in `xyz2ccf`. At 10 µm the volume is exactly symmetric about 5695 µm, the
plane between voxels 569 and 570, and the score drops steadily on both sides of it. The 25 and 50 µm
volumes are resampled from it and peak within 5 µm of it, the precision of their voxel grid. Bregma
at 5739 µm is a clearly worse mirror plane than the midline.

| ML mirror plane (µm) | 10 µm: overlap / correlation | 25 µm: overlap / correlation | 50 µm: overlap / correlation |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 5639 (bregma − 100) | 0.952 / 0.776 | 0.954 / 0.780 | 0.952 / 0.796 |
| 5675 | 0.982 / 0.930 | 0.984 / 0.934 | 0.982 / 0.928 |
| 5685 | 0.991 / 0.975 | 0.993 / 0.981 | 0.987 / 0.977 |
| 5690 | 0.995 / 0.992 | **0.995** / 0.993 | 0.990 / 0.990 |
| **5695** | **1.000 / 1.000** | 0.994 / **0.997** | 0.993 / **0.995** |
| 5700 | 0.995 / 0.992 | 0.993 / 0.991 | **0.995** / 0.992 |
| 5705 | 0.991 / 0.975 | 0.989 / 0.979 | 0.991 / 0.985 |
| 5715 | 0.982 / 0.930 | 0.980 / 0.936 | 0.982 / 0.947 |
| 5739 (IBL bregma) | 0.962 / 0.823 | 0.960 / 0.829 | 0.961 / 0.843 |

: Similarity of the two sides of the Allen volumes mirrored about different ML positions. The best
score of each column is in bold. The 10 µm volumes were decimated by 4 along AP and DV to fit in
memory. {#tbl-midline}

## The five atlases

Which atlas fits depends on where your coordinates come from.

| Your coordinates | Atlas |
|---|---|
| Histology, or a tool that registers data to the Allen CCF | **Allen** |
| A planned probe insertion, or stereotaxic coordinates on a live mouse | **Needles** or **MRI Toronto** |
| A plan made in Pinpoint's Dorr 2008 or Qiu 2018 space | **Dorr 2008** or **Qiu 2018** |

## Coordinates from histology: the Allen atlas

The Allen atlas is the Allen CCF, an average of 1,675 mouse brains imaged by serial two-photon
tomography. Histology and registration tools place data in the CCF, so their coordinates are in
the Allen atlas. Its region annotations are the Allen 2017 release.

## Planning an insertion: the Needles, MRI Toronto, Dorr 2008 and Qiu 2018 atlases

Stereotaxic coordinates are measured from bregma with the brain inside the skull. The Needles
and MRI Toronto atlases stretch the Allen CCF along each axis to fit an MRI atlas of the brain
in the skull, so their coordinates are closer to those used in surgery. The Dorr 2008 and Qiu 2018
atlases have the same two scalings and add a pitch.

::: {.column-body-outset}

| Atlas | Pinpoint name | Source               | Acquisition | Subjects | ML ratio | AP ratio | DV ratio | Pitch |
|--------|-----------|----------------------|-------------|-------------|------|------|------|-----|
| **Needles** | `IBL-Dorr2008` | Dorr 2008 (DSURQE) with no pitch | Post-mortem, brain in skull | 40 C57BL/6J, p84 | 1 | 1.087 | 0.952 | none |
| **MRI Toronto** | none | Qiu 2018             | In vivo | 12, p65 | 0.952 | 1.031 | 0.885 | none |
| **Dorr 2008** | `Dorr2008` | Dorr 2008 (DSURQE)   | Post-mortem, brain in skull | 40 C57BL/6J, p84 | 1 | 1.087 | 0.952 | 5° |
| **Qiu 2018** | `Qiu2018` | Qiu 2018             | In vivo | 12, p65 | 0.952 | 1.031 | 0.885 | 5° |

:::

### The 5° pitch: the Dorr 2008 and Qiu 2018 atlases

`Qiu2018Atlas` is `MRITorontoAtlas` and `Dorr2008Atlas` is `NeedlesAtlas`, each followed by a
rotation of 5° about the ML axis, with bregma as the pivot. They follow the Qiu 2018 and Dorr 2008
transforms of [Pinpoint](https://virtualbrainlab.org/pinpoint/in_vivo_alignment.html), which rotate
the CCF to level the bregma-lambda surface, pitching it up by 5° (Birman et al. 2023, citing the
International Brain Laboratory). Pinpoint's legacy IBL Dorr transform is the Needles scaling
alone, which is `NeedlesAtlas`. @fig-slices shows the Qiu 2018 atlas beside the unpitched ones.

- The scaling is applied first, then the rotation. Bregma is the pivot, so it stays at `(0, 0, 0)`.
- A positive `pitch`, in degrees, lifts the anterior side of the atlas: `pitch=5.0` is the
  default of both atlases. The direction follows Pinpoint's description of the rotation, and has not been
  checked against a lambda coordinate.
- The rotation is in the atlas coordinates, not in the volumes. The image and annotation volumes
  are those of the Allen CCF, so data on the CCF grid stays aligned with the atlas.
- Converting points works: `xyz2ccf`, `ccf2xyz` and `get_labels` go through the rotation.
  Anything that needs the brain surface or the voxel size of an axis raises a `ValueError`,
  because the volume axes no longer line up with the atlas axes: the slice and surface plots
  (`plot_sslice`, `plot_top`, `compute_surface`), `get_labels(radius_um=...)` and the `Insertion`
  methods that use the surface (`Insertion.from_dict`, `get_brain_entry`). To draw a pitched
  slice, look the labels up on a grid of coordinates with `get_labels`, as @fig-slices does. See
  [Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd#atlases-with-a-rotation).

The three voxels marked P1 to P3 in @fig-slices, to check a conversion. Each row is one CCF voxel and its position in
each atlas, in (ML, AP, DV) µm, relative to bregma for the atlases and from the corner of the
volume for the CCF.

| Point | Region | CCF | Allen | Needles | MRI Toronto | Qiu 2018 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | onl | 5739, 1400, 4332 | 0, 4000, -4000 | 0, 4348, -3808 | 0, 4124, -3540 | 0, 4417, -3167 |
| P2 | SF | 5739, 5400, 3332 | 0, 0, -3000 | 0, 0, -2856 | 0, 0, -2655 | 0, 231, -2645 |
| P3 | CENT3 | 5739, 11400, 3332 | 0, -6000, -3000 | 0, -6522, -2856 | 0, -6186, -2655 | 0, -5931, -3184 |

[Pinpoint](https://virtualbrainlab.org/pinpoint/in_vivo_alignment.html) is the tool many IBL
users plan in vivo trajectories with. For the Allen atlas it offers four transforms: `Default`
(no scaling), `Qiu2018`, `Dorr2008` and `IBL-Dorr2008`. The table above gives the matching atlases.
Check that an `Insertion` and a Pinpoint plan are expressed in the same frame before comparing
them. State which tool produced a coordinate when you record it.
